t:
(a) None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act may be used to determine the final point of discharge for the interceptor drain for the San Luis Unit until development by the Secretary of the Interior and the State of California of a plan, which shall conform to the water quality 
standards of the State of California as approved by the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, to minimize any detrimental effect of the San Luis drainage waters. 
    (b) The costs of the Kesterson Reservoir Cleanup Program and the costs of the San Joaquin Valley Drainage Program shall be classified by the Secretary of the Interior as reimbursable or nonreimbursable and collected until fully repaid pursuant to the “Cleanup Program—Alternative Repayment Plan” and the “SJVDP—Alternative Repayment Plan” described in the report entitled “Repayment Report, Kesterson Reservoir Cleanup Program and San Joaquin Valley Drainage Program, February 1995”, prepared by the Department of the Interior, Bureau of Reclamation. Any future obligations of funds by the United States relating to, or providing for, drainage service or drainage studies for the San Luis Unit shall be fully reimbursable by San Luis Unit beneficiaries of such service or studies pursuant to Federal reclamation law.

fable.w: The federal decision on the final point of discharge for the San Luis interceptor drain cannot be made until the Secretary of the Interior and the State of California jointly develop a plan. California is outside the federal government, so this is required coordination with a state before a federal action. The tempting reading is that this is only an appropriations restriction plus intra-federal EPA approval and cost-reimbursement rules, but the joint plan requirement brings the state into the decision.
fable.s: until development by the Secretary of the Interior and the State of California of a plan

opus.w: The Secretary of the Interior can't decide the final point of discharge for the San Luis interceptor drain until the Secretary and the State of California have developed a plan together. A state is outside the federal government, so this is required coordination with an outside party before a federal decision. The opposite reading fails: the appropriations language and EPA's approval of the standards are federal-only, but they don't remove the State's role in shaping the plan that must come before the decision.
opus.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act may be used to determine the final point of discharge for the interceptor drain for the San Luis Unit until development by the Secretary of the Interior and the State of California of a plan
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is just a funding restriction, or that the EPA approval is the only process involved, and EPA is inside the federal government. That reading misses that subsection (a) makes a federal decision (setting the final discharge point) wait on a plan developed jointly with the State of California, which is an outside party.
